title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو يحذر من الفتن ويدعو إلى الوحدةوإصلاح ذات البين
title_en: His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew Warns against Discord and Calls for Unity and the Mending of Relations
body_ar:
حذر فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو في خطبة الجمعة التى ألقاها يوم أمس 7 أكتوبر 2011 بمجمع أسامة بن زيد حذر من خطر الفتن التى تتهدد المجتمع الموريتاني وعلى رأس تلك الفتن فتنة الرفض والتشيع ...وقال حفظه الله لا خير في من يعادى أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويطعنون فيهم فلذالك احذروهم ولا تستمعوا إليهم .

من جهة أخرى دعا فضيلة الشيخ في نفس الخطبة إلى و حدة الصف وإصلاح ذات البين وإلى الإيثار بالحقوق وإلى أن يتنازل كل طرف عن ما يراه حقا له مقابل إصلاح ذات البين ، وتأتى هذه الدعوة على خلفية الأحداث الأليمة التى شهدتها مدينة نواكشوط وبعض مدن الداخل وكادت تعصف بالوحدة الوطنية والانسجام الأهلي .

لمتابعة خطبة فضيلة الشيخ اضغط هنا :

http://dedewnet.com/index.php/dawa/khotab-jomoa.html?view=media&id=1562
body_en:
In the Friday sermon he delivered yesterday, 7 October 2011, at the Usamah ibn Zayd complex, His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew warned of the danger of the trials that threaten Mauritanian society, and at the head of those trials the trial of Rejectionism (al-rafḍ) and Shi'ism (al-tashayyuʿ)… He said, may God preserve him: there is no good in one who shows enmity to the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and who impugn them; so beware of them and do not listen to them.

On another matter, in the same sermon His Eminence the Sheikh called for unity of the ranks and for the mending of relations, and for preferring others in the matter of rights, and for each party to give up what it regards as its right for the sake of mending relations. This call comes against the background of the painful events the city of Nouakchott and some towns of the interior have witnessed, which came close to sweeping away national unity and communal harmony.

flags.arabic: وعلى رأس تلك الفتن فتنة الرفض والتشيع ...وقال حفظه الله لا خير في من يعادى أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويطعنون فيهم فلذالك احذروهم ولا تستمعوا إليهم
flags.context: the whole of the first paragraph
options: translate faithfully and hold for an editorial decision
flags.note: CRITICAL — editorial_review. Style guide section 12. This is a named scholar, reported as naming a religious community as the foremost danger to his society and telling his congregation to beware of its members and not to listen to them. الرفض is a polemical term for Twelver Shi'ism and it is rendered here as what it is, 'Rejectionism', rather than softened to a neutral description or strengthened by a gloss the Arabic does not carry. Published in English, this is a passage capable of being read as incitement against a religious minority, and in several jurisdictions in which Ummah Collective may publish it carries legal as well as reputational exposure. The decision whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office and to no one else. Note that fifteen words of a sermon, in a journalist's paraphrase, is the whole of what survives here.

flags.context: the naming of the trial at the head of the list
options: the trial of Rejectionism (al-rafḍ) and Shi'ism (al-tashayyuʿ)
flags.note: Two words, not one, and the English must keep both. الرفض / الروافض is a polemical term of art for Twelver Shi'ism used by its opponents; التشيع is the ordinary word for Shi'ism. Collapsing them into 'Shi'ism' would drop the polemical register the Arabic has, and rendering the pair as something vaguer would soften a position the style guide forbids softening. The three ellipsis dots after التشيع are the source's own and mark an omission in the news desk's paraphrase, not in this translation.

flags.arabic: وقال حفظه الله لا خير في من يعادى أصحاب رسول الله … ويطعنون فيهم
flags.context: the sentence given as the Sheikh's own words
options: translate as it stands, keeping the shift from singular to plural
render the whole in the plural
flags.note: The Arabic moves from a singular relative (من يعادى) to a plural verb (ويطعنون فيهم) and then to a plural imperative addressed to the congregation (احذروهم). The shift is preserved rather than smoothed, because it is the point at which the sentence stops describing a type of person and starts telling the audience what to do about a group of people, and smoothing it would blur exactly what a reviewer needs to see. Note also that the sentence carries no quotation marks in the source, so how much of it is the Sheikh's wording and how much the reporter's is not determinable from this record.

flags.arabic: الأحداث الأليمة التى شهدتها مدينة نواكشوط وبعض مدن الداخل
flags.context: the background to the call for unity
options: render as given, with no identification of the events
identify the events in an editorial note
flags.note: The report does not say what the events were, and the translator must not supply an identification. Without it, an English reader cannot tell whether the second paragraph's call for unity is addressed to the same situation as the first paragraph's warning or to a separate one. That ambiguity is in the Arabic and is preserved.

translator_notes: This is a news report of a sermon, written by the site's news desk. The whole of it is two paragraphs; the sermon itself exists as audio at the link recorded in source_download_link.

critical_for_display. A reader meeting this in English will take the two reported positions for the Sheikh's sermon, when what survives is a reporter's compression of it with no quotation marks around most of it and the source's own ellipsis marking material dropped. The site must not render this as a fatwa or as his text.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written. The body dates the sermon to Friday 7 October 2011, which is consistent.
إصلاح ذات البين is rendered 'the mending of relations'. It is a Qur'anic phrase (Sūrat al-Anfāl 8:1) and is not quoted as such here, so no locator is given.
الإيثار بالحقوق is rendered 'preferring others in the matter of rights' — that is, yielding one's own entitlement to another. It is not a ruling word and takes no part in the five-rulings mapping.

The title's الوحدةوإصلاح is run together without a space in the source; the space is restored in the English title only, and title_ar preserves the source spelling. The body's و حدة is likewise split in the source.
The closing 'click here' line and the bare URL under it are the site's navigation furniture; preserved in body_ar, recorded in source_download_link, omitted from body_en.
dec: Names a religious community as the foremost danger to its society and tells the congregation to beware of its members. Capable of being read as incitement against a minority.
